newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay's latest Airbus arrives.
newsitem.headline: Cathay's latest Airbus arrives.

text.p: HONG KONG Feb 12. (Reuter) Cathay Pacific Airways Limited completed the latest part of its fleet modernisation programme Wednesday with the arrival in Hong Kong of its newest aircraft from Airbus, an airline spokeswoman told Reuters.

The A340-300 will be used on Cathay's ultra long haul routes from Hong Kong to Toronto, Zurich, Rome and Melbourne (with Auckland and Johannesburg in the near future) in addition to short haul regional destinations including Japan and the Philippines.

Up to 33 LD3 belly hold cargo containers and 261 passengers in three classes can be carried. It is the last of six A340-300s and 11 A330-300s which have now fully replaced Cathay's veteran Lockheed Tristar fleet.

Cathay management have said the new Airbus fleet offers air cargo opportunities by being able to fly between 15 and 17 tonnes of belly space cargo plus passengers compared with just eight tonnes in the now retired Tristars.
The arrival also means the last of Cathay's leased Airbus A340- 200 aircraft will be returned next month, the spokeswoman added.

The latest delivery, which brings Cathay's current fleet total to 60 airliners, is the last for more than a year. The Hong Kong airline still has 13 new aircraft on order valued at $2 billion and 25 on option worth another $4 billion.
But the seven Boeing 777- 300, five Airbus A340-300 and one A330-300 on order will not start to arrive until after the scheduled opening in April next year of Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport.
Cathay management have said they hope to take full advantage of their new home base which will offer round the clock access without slot restrictions to the airline's expanded fleet.

According to Cathay statistics, the airline expects to carry more than 11 million passengers this year compared to 10.985 million in 1996, 10.381 millinn in 1995 and 9.750 million in 1994. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
